A.depoimento: We launch a dual-pronged assault on the nearby neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to secure our first stepping stones into the wider world. Our forces split from the capital to overwhelm the local garrisons and claim their resources for the crown.
A.plano: Our immediate goal is to secure the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora to establish an economic foothold and expand our territory. Once these are captured, we will use them as launching points to explore the unexplored regions to the north and east, mapping out the enemy's position and securing more villages to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

B.depoimento: I order the construction of 2 spearmen and send my entire army of 5 spearmen, 4 archers, and 3 knights to attack the neutral village of Tarragona. The spearman counter bonus should give me a decisive advantage. I aim to capture the village and begin my expansion towards Zaragoza.
B.plano: Build 2 spearmen in Barcelona. Send all 12 current troops to attack Tarragona (21). The spearmen counter the knight garrison. Next turn, check the battle outcome, build in Tarragona if captured, and consider marching on Zaragoza (17).

A.depoimento: King A's armies march on Coimbra and Faro today, determined to claim these lands for our people. Our forces move with speed and purpose, while the capital forges a new knight to strengthen our ranks. Reinforcements are sent to our frontier villages to ensure our hold remains firm. We trust in our generals and the righteousness of our cause. Victory shall be ours!
A.plano: Our immediate campaign is to conquer the neutral villages of Coimbra and Faro to expand our territory and resources. We will attack Coimbra from Santarem and Faro from Evora with our full garrisons. In the capital Lisboa, we will build a knight to bolster our military strength and send spearman reinforcements to Santarem and Evora to hold the line. Once Coimbra and Faro are ours, we will use them as bases to push north towards Porto and Salamanca, and south towards Sevilha and Badajoz, aiming to surround and isolate the enemy capital at Barcelona. We will continue building troops in our villag

B.depoimento: Tarragona's full army marches on Castellon to crush the knight garrison. I reinforce Tarragona with spearmen from the capital while a knight is forged in Barcelona, ready to pounce on Girona next turn. My expansion begins with fire and steel!
B.plano: Attack Castellon with all of Tarragona's forces to secure a southern foothold. Reinforce Tarragona with the spearmen from Barcelona. Build a knight in Barcelona; next turn, use it to capture Girona (knight counters the archer garrison). Continue expanding along the coast and towards Zaragoza.

A.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the full garrisons of Faro and Coimbra to attack Badajoz and Porto, respectively, seeking to capture these valuable neutral villages and increase our strength. I also sent reinforcements from Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to support our advancing forces and secure our new territories. In our villages, we built new troops to prepare for the next phase of our expansion.
A.plano: Our campaign is to conquer the neutral villages of Badajoz and Porto this turn to expand our territory and resource production. After capturing them, we will build up our armies in the core villages and prepare to push north to Salamanca and south to Sevilha. We will also explore the unexplored regions to locate the enemy capital and aim to surround Barcelona. We will maintain a balanced mix of spearman, archer, and knights to counter the enemy's forces.

B.depoimento: Order is restored in the south! Having secured Castellon, my forces now strike at Valencia with archers and knights, while my capital's knight rides to take Girona. Tarragona's spearmen march to reinforce Castellon, and my villages bustle with production. The coast is mine, and the road to the north opens.
B.plano: We captured Castellon last turn. This turn, we build a knight in Barcelona and send it to capture Girona. We build 2 spearmen in Tarragona and send the existing 2 spearmen to reinforce Castellon. From Castellon, we send 4 archers and 3 knights to capture Valencia. This expands our territory to 5 villages (Barcelona, Tarragona, Castellon, Valencia, Girona) and secures our southern flank. Next turn, we should look to expand towards Zaragoza and Teruel, and build more troops in our new villages.

A.depoimento: I have consolidated my hold on Badajoz and Porto, and now I strike against the neutral villages of Toledo and Vigo. My armies move from Badajoz and Porto, while my interior villages work to build a steady stream of reinforcements. The expansion continues.
A.plano: My campaign focuses on conquering the neutral villages to expand my territory and resources. This turn, I attack Toledo from Badajoz and Vigo from Porto. Next turn, I will target Salamanca and Sevilha, using the newly captured villages as staging points. I am building reinforcements in my core villages to maintain momentum. I will also explore the unexplored regions to locate the enemy capital and other enemy villages. My goal is to reach 18 villages or eliminate all enemies.

B.depoimento: King B's armies strike twice! The spearman of Castellon charge at Teruel, while the archers of Valencia march on Murcia. Our knights reinforce the flanks, and the forges work overtime to build more spearman. The net of villages is tightening around the enemy capital!
B.plano: We launched a double offensive on Teruel and Murcia to expand our territory to 7 villages. Castellon sent 7 spearman to Teruel, and Valencia sent 4 archers to Murcia. We reinforced Castellon with 3 knights from Valencia and Tarragona with 1 knight from Barcelona. We built 2 spearman in Barcelona, Tarragona, and Castellon to grow our army. Next turn, we must prepare to attack Zaragoza from Tarragona and push towards Madrid, while securing our newly conquered lands.

A.depoimento: My armies have secured Toledo and Vigo, expanding my realm. Today, I strike at Sevilha, sending my finest archers and knights from Badajoz to break the neutral garrison. Reinforcements are being trained across my lands to sustain the march.
A.plano: My campaign focuses on conquering the neutral villages to expand my territory and resources. This turn, I attack Sevilha from Badajoz with 3 archers and 1 knight, expecting to win and conquer it. Next turn, I will use Sevilha as a staging point to attack Cordoba. I am building reinforcements in my core villages, particularly knights in Lisboa and spearmen in others, to maintain momentum and prepare for attacks on Salamanca and Madrid. My goal is to reach 18 villages or eliminate all enemies.

B.depoimento: This turn we consolidate and prepare. Reinforcements from Castellon and Barcelona flow into Tarragona, building a mighty force to strike Zaragoza. In Girona, an archer is raised to counter Huesca's spearmen. Murcia's archers are redeployed to Valencia, while our spearmen already on the march assault Teruel. The path to the north opens.
B.plano: Reinforcing Tarragona for a Zaragoza attack next turn. Girona builds an archer to counter Huesca's spearmen. Murcia's archers move to Valencia for safety and future operations. The 7 spearmen should take Teruel this turn. Do not attack Zaragoza now (lack of knights). Do not send Girona's knight alone to Huesca (would lose). Focus on the northern expansion.

A.depoimento: We are reinforcing our borders and building troops to launch attacks on the neutral villages. We send knights to Toledo and spearmen to Badajoz to strengthen our positions.
A.plano: We are building up our army and sending reinforcements to our border villages to prepare for attacks on the neutral villages. We will focus on conquering Salamanca, Cordoba, Madrid, and Burgos to expand our territory. We send knights to Toledo and spearmen to Badajoz to strengthen our positions. Next turn, we will use these reinforced villages to launch attacks on the nearest neutrals.

B.depoimento: We strike on two fronts this turn! Tarragona's knights march on Zaragoza, while Girona's archer and knight assault Huesca. Simultaneously, we reinforce Teruel with Valencia's archers and Castellon's knight, setting up a powerful strike against the enemy's Toledo next turn. Our villages continue to produce knights and archers to fuel our expansion.
B.plano: Capture Zaragoza with Tarragona's knights and Huesca with Girona's troops. Reinforce Teruel with Valencia's archers and Castellon's knight to launch a strong counter-attack on Toledo next turn. Focus on northern and central expansion while securing our borders.

A.depoimento: King A's forces launched a coordinated offensive on the neutral villages. Salamanca fell to Coimbra's spearmen, Cordoba was assaulted by Toledo's knights, and a mixed army marched on Madrid. Meanwhile, Badajoz sent spearmen to reinforce our border capital Toledo, and we began building troops across our realm for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: We are capturing the neutral villages of Salamanca, Cordoba, and Madrid to expand our territory and reach the 18-village threshold. Our Coimbra spearmen take Salamanca, Toledo's knights strike Cordoba, and a mixed force advances on Madrid. Badajoz reinforces Toledo to secure our border against the enemy at Teruel. After these captures, we will target Burgos and the unexplored eastern villages, building more spearmen and knights to maintain momentum and eliminate enemy strongholds.

B.depoimento: Turn 7 is about to begin. I am launching a double strike: Zaragoza's knights will take Madrid, while a carefully mixed force from Teruel—led by archers to exploit the counter bonus against Toledo's spearmen—will assault the enemy stronghold. I am also reinforcing our southern flank by sending a knight from Valencia to Murcia and another from Castellon to Teruel, while our home villages focus on building knights and spearmen to sustain the momentum of our expansion.
B.plano: Capture Madrid with Zaragoza's knights and Toledo with Teruel's mixed force using the archer counter bonus. Reinforce Murcia with Valencia's knight and Teruel with Castellon's knight. Build up our economy and army in all villages to prepare for further expansion towards Pamplona and Cordoba next turn.

A.depoimento:
This turn, we strengthen our borders by sending troops to Cordoba and Toledo.
Our spearmen assault Salamanca while our forces attack Madrid.
We build knights across the realm to prepare for the next phase.
We are determined to expand our kingdom and win.
A.plano:
This turn, our armies capture Salamanca and Madrid, reaching 13 villages.
We reinforce Cordoba and Toledo to secure our borders.
Next, we will consolidate, then attack Burgos with knights and Murcia with spearmen.
We will explore the east to find enemy weaknesses and work toward holding 18 villages or destroying King B.

B.depoimento: This turn, we marched to war. We attacked Burgos with Madrid's knights and Cordoba with Murcia's forces, sacrificing Madrid to strengthen our western expansion. We reinforced Zaragoza and Teruel, and built up our archer and knight forces for the next phase.
B.plano: Plan: Sacrificed Madrid to attack Burgos and reinforced Zaragoza with troops from Tarragona and Huesca. Attacked Cordoba with Murcia's knights. Built archers and knights to prepare for expansion. Next turn: assess battles, consolidate new villages, and prepare to attack Pamplona from Huesca with archers.

A.depoimento: Our armies converge on Burgos, overwhelming the enemy garrison. Reinforcements flow to the front as we prepare for the next phase of our campaign.
A.plano: We are launching a major attack on Burgos with forces from Vigo and Madrid. After capturing it, we will explore north to find more villages and push toward the enemy capital. We are reinforcing our borders and building up spearmen and knights for future offensives. Our goal is to quickly reach 18 villages and secure victory.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies struck at the weak points of the enemy, taking Murcia and Pamplona. While the enemy is distracted, we are massing our forces at Toledo and Madrid for the decisive blows against Teruel and Zaragoza. The net of our conquest is tightening.
A.plano: We are taking Murcia and Pamplona this turn to reach 16 villages. We are sending all available troops from interior to the borders of Toledo and Madrid to prepare for attacks on Teruel and Zaragoza next turn. We are building spearmen, archers, and knights across our empire to grow our army. Our goal is to conquer Teruel and Zaragoza next turn to reach 18 villages and secure victory.

B.depoimento: I am building up my forces across all villages, focusing on archers and knights. I am sending a fast strike force from Zaragoza to capture the neutral village of Pamplona, which will give me my 10th village and improve my position.
B.plano: Build archers and knights in all villages to maximize mobile firepower. Attack the neutral village Pamplona from Zaragoza using archers and knights to exploit the counter bonus, leaving spearmen in Zaragoza for defense. Monitor Murcia's vulnerability to Cordoba.

B.depoimento: Turn 11: I am consolidating my borders. I am sending massive reinforcements from Tarragona and Huesca to Zaragoza, and from Zaragoza to the vulnerable Pamplona. I am moving Valencia's troops to Murcia to prepare a decisive strike on Cordoba next turn. I am building archers and knights across all my villages to strengthen my army.
B.plano: Reinforce Zaragoza from Tarragona and Huesca, and send Zaragoza's troops to Pamplona to defend it from Burgos. Send Valencia's troops to Murcia to prepare for the attack on Cordoba next turn. Build archers and knights everywhere to grow our army. Do not attack Cordoba this turn; wait for reinforcements.

A.depoimento: We have launched a decisive attack on Pamplona, committing our entire Burgos force to overwhelm the enemy. Meanwhile, we are building up our armies, constructing archers and knights in our border cities and dispatching reinforcements to Toledo, Cordoba, Madrid, and Burgos. The army gathering at Toledo will soon march on Teruel. We are confident these actions will lead us to victory.
A.plano: This turn we assault Pamplona with the Burgos garrison to capture our 15th village. We are building archers at Toledo, Cordoba, Madrid and knights across our realm. We send reinforcements to Toledo (knights and archers) to prepare for an attack on Teruel next turn. We also reinforce Madrid, Cordoba, and Burgos for future offensives. After taking Pamplona, we will strike Huesca. Our goal is to reach 18 villages and hold them for two turns to win.

B.depoimento: Our armies strike. In the south, archers rain down on Cordoba, their counter attack shattering the enemy. From the east, reinforcements pour into Pamplona, strengthening our northern bulwark. Every village forges archers, feeding the war machine. We advance on all fronts.
B.plano: Attack Cordoba with archers to counter their spearmen and exploit their weak defense. Reinforce Pamplona from Zaragoza and Huesca to secure the north against Burgos. Send Valencia's archer to Murcia to bolster its defense after the attack. Move Castellon's troops to Teruel to prepare for the assault on Toledo. Build archers in all villages to replace losses and grow our army. Focus on the south first, then pivot to Madrid and Toledo.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launch a decisive assault on Cordoba with Toledo's elite knights and archers to reclaim our lost territory. We are mobilizing our entire realm, building knights in every capable village and marching reinforcements to our border strongholds of Toledo, Madrid, and Burgos. Our sights are set on securing Cordoba first, then consolidating our forces to strike at Teruel and Zaragoza.
A.plano: We are attacking Cordoba with Toledo's knights and archers to recapture our lost village. We are building knights in almost all our villages to build up our offensive power. We are sending reinforcements from Badajoz, Lisboa, Santarem, Evora, and Faro to Toledo, and from Salamanca, Coimbra, and Porto to Madrid. We also send knights from Vigo to Burgos and Sevilha to Cordoba to secure our gains. Next turn, we will consolidate our forces in Toledo and Madrid to prepare for attacks on Teruel and Zaragoza.

B.depoimento: This turn, we struck at Burgos with archers, leveraging the counter to overcome their defenses. We reinforced Pamplona from Huesca and Zaragoza to hold the north. In the south, we moved Murcia's army to Cordoba to prepare for the push on Sevilha, while building spearmen there. We also sent troops from the eastern villages to Zaragoza and Teruel, building our strength for the coming battles. Our forces are growing, and we press the advantage.
B.plano: We attacked Burgos with archers from Pamplona to exploit their weak defense and counter their spearmen. Reinforcements from Huesca and Zaragoza will arrive to secure Pamplona. We sent all of Murcia's troops to Cordoba to prepare for the assault on Sevilha next turn, building spearmen there to counter their knights. We also sent troops from the eastern villages to Zaragoza and Teruel to build up forces for future attacks on Madrid and Toledo. Next turn, we will attack Sevilha with spearmen from Cordoba and continue pressing the north. We must watch for enemy counterattacks on Pamplona and Cordo

A.depoimento: This turn, we coordinate a major offensive on the eastern front. Our forces in Toledo march on Teruel, while Madrid strikes at Zaragoza. Simultaneously, Cordoba's garrison cleans up the vulnerable village of Murcia. We are also focusing on domestic production, building spearments across our realm to ensure our armies remain replenished.
A.plano: We are launching a three-pronged attack this turn. From Toledo, we send knights and archers to attack Teruel. From Madrid, we send knights and archers to attack Zaragoza. From Cordoba, we send all troops to attack the weak Murcia. We are building 2 spearmen in almost all our villages to replenish our ranks and maintain our economy. Our goal is to conquer Murcia, Teruel, and Zaragoza to push our village count towards the 18 needed for victory.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch an assault on Burgos with our Pamplona garrison, aiming to conquer this weak enemy village and push our borders north. We reinforce Pamplona with a large contingent from Zaragoza to ensure we hold the line, and we move troops from Valencia to Murcia to build up our southern front for the push toward Cordoba. Across the empire, we are busy producing knights and archers to strengthen our forces for the challenges ahead.
B.plano: We are attacking the weakly defended Burgos from Pamplona to expand our territory and secure the northern border. We are reinforcing Pamplona with troops from Zaragoza to maintain a strong garrison after the attack. In the south, we are moving troops from Valencia to Murcia to prepare for an upcoming assault on Cordoba. We are building knights and archers across all our villages to grow our army for future attacks on Madrid and Toledo.

A.depoimento: This turn, we strike on two fronts to claim our 18th and 19th villages! From Teruel, our forces overwhelm Valencia, while from Zaragoza, our knights and spearmen crush Huesca. We reinforce Zaragoza from Madrid to hold the line, and we build 2 spearmen in every village to swell our ranks. With 18 villages in our grasp, we march toward victory!
A.plano: We are launching a two-pronged attack this turn to conquer Valencia and Huesca, which will bring our total to 18 villages. From Teruel, we send all troops to attack the weak Valencia. From Zaragoza, we send all troops to attack Huesca. We are reinforcing Zaragoza with 15 spearmen from Madrid to secure the border. We are building 2 spearmen in all our villages to replenish our ranks and maintain our economy. Our goal is to conquer Valencia and Huesca this turn, and then hold our 18 villages for the next turn to secure victory.

B.depoimento: I'm sending Burgos's five archers to take Vigo - a village held by barely two spearmen - while leaving three spearmen behind as a reserve. I built troops in all eight villages to rebuild the army after two armies were lost last turn. A big reinforcement is due at Pamplona next turn and should finally give us the punch to threaten Zaragoza.
B.plano: Turn 16 plan: attack Vigo[10] from Burgos with 5 archers (def 5, only 2 spearmen) for my 9th village; keep 3 spearmen at Burgos as a reserve. Building everywhere: 3 knights, 2 archers, 8 spearmen to rebuild the army after last turn's losses. Big reinforcement (4s/5a/5k) arrives at Pamplona next turn. Then push Vigo->Porto or mass for Zaragoza/Madrid. Watch: Valencia (1 knight) and Castellon look thin on the southern border.

A.depoimento: Our knights descend on Girona! We strike with precision and power. Our borders grow stronger as we march to victory.
A.plano: Attack Girona from Huesca with 4 knights and 1 archer to secure our 18th village. Reinforce Porto from Coimbra/Salamanca, Teruel from Toledo, Valencia from Murcia. Build troops in all villages to maintain army. Hold new territory for victory.

B.depoimento: My armies strike at the weak enemy village of Teruel, claiming my eighth territory. I strengthen my borders with spearmen and knights, while my forges burn day and night. The enemy may try to exploit my momentary weakness at Castellon, but I will not yield. On to victory!
B.plano: Attacking Teruel with 2 archers from Castellon to secure 8th village. Reinforcing Girona (2s from Barcelona), Vigo (2s from Burgos), and Burgos (2s/2a/1k from Pamplona) to prepare for next attacks. Building knights in all 6 border villages and 2 spear in Barcelona. Next turn: attack Porto from Vigo with combined force; continue building for push towards Madrid. Watch Castellon's defense after attack; consider reinforcing from Tarragona if safe.

A.depoimento: This turn, I fortified our vulnerable borders by sending reinforcements to Girona, Zaragoza, Huesca, and Teruel. I also ordered a massive build of 1 knight and 2 spearmen in every single village to swell our ranks and prepare for the next phase of the war.
A.plano: Reinforce the northern and eastern borders to secure our 18-village majority. Send troops from Madrid to Zaragoza, Zaragoza to Huesca, Huesca to Girona, and Toledo to Teruel to fortify against enemy capitals and border villages. Simultaneously, build a balanced army of knights and spearman in all 18 villages to grow our core military strength. Hold the line and prepare for a counter-offensive once our borders are secure.

B.depoimento: Turn 18: I launch a double attack. Barcelona's army strikes Girona, while Pamplona's forces march on Huesca. My villages work overtime, forging knights and archers to swell my ranks. The enemy will not expect such swift action on two fronts.
B.plano: Attack Girona [23] from Barcelona [22] with all available troops (2 spearman, 3 knight) to capture it in 1 turn. Send Pamplona [19] troops (6 spearman, 5 archer, 4 knight) to Huesca [20] to capture it in 2 turns. Build knights in Barcelona, Castellon, Burgos, Vigo; archers in Tarragona, Pamplona to grow army. Focus on expanding north/east.
